A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a novel distributed algorithm for maintaining the rigidity property for a team of robots using only range measurements and a bearing measurement for one agent.

we propose a fully decentralized rigidity maintenance control strategy for multi-robot system with range measurements, while allowing the graph topology and sensing/communication ranges to change freely.
we have developed a distributed algorithm for maintaining the rigidity of the multi-robot system while also enforcing other additional constraints.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a fully decentralized rigidity maintenance control scheme can be achieved for multi-robot teams using only local range measurements and a single robot capable of measuring the bearing angles to two other agents, without requiring a global reference frame, nor any global communication.
a fully decentralized rigidity maintenance strategy for multi-robot formations using only range measurements is feasible and can be implemented with a practical robotic system.

rigidity can be maintained even in the presence of range-only measurements, while allowing the robots to change their relative position over time, which can be of great importance in applications where the robots are required to move in order to perform their tasks.
